notes.title: Patch 1.2.0
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=DLsb0LStbYY;full][/previewyoutube]
New Content
Cannon
The Cannon is a new Epic block that launches items into a block or onto a tile ahead of it. It comes with the new card "Extra Gunpowder" and reduces the necessity of conveyors. With this, the potential of larger mechanisms skyrockets, as automation will be much easier.

Teleporter
The Teleporter is a new Legendary block that teleports items and players from one teleporter to another. It can be used both to receive and send items, so it can be used to save lots of space in the cave. It also comes with the card "Overclocking." Teleporters must be connected in pairs.

Safe
The Safe is a new block that is exclusive to the shop in the Infinite and Pure Chaos game modes. Its purpose is to display the chances of each rarity in the shop's stock. It also allows players to increase the chances of higher rarity blocks, or decrease the chances of lower rarity blocks. The price for upgrading the shop is not final and may be adjusted in future patches.

Steam Remote Play
Steam Remote Play was previously disabled for Compactory, which forced players to use 3rd party services to play Local Multiplayer remotely. So, by popular request, Steam Remote Play is now enabled for Compactory. Although this isn't Online Multiplayer, it provides an opportunity for those who are willing to play Local Multiplayer remotely. Online Multiplayer is coming in the next patch!


Balance Changes
Dynamite Rework
Previously, Dynamite seemed weak for its main purpose: to destroy blocks. It was limited to destroying blocks that accepted items because dynamite was originally designed as an Item.
However, in this patch, Dynamite was redesigned as a Tool and can now destroy any blocks surrounding it. It still remains at the same price and rarity, but now it has four times the value, if not more for being able to destroy ores. Just be careful to not accidentally destroy something important!

Quota Scaling
Many players found the scaling of the quota to be too difficult before this patch. Especially in single-player, it felt impossible to keep up with the ever-increasing quota while trying to build a strategy.
As a result, the quota was readjusted to scale more dramatically only in the latest rounds before Round 20. This way, players who were lucky enough to reach later rounds will be challenged by the higher quotas, while players in the earlier rounds will still be given room to grow. The new quota scaling may be adjusted in future patches.

Alloy Rework
Before this patch, all Alloys seemed too weak compared to their ingredients. There was no incentive for an alloy setup when players already had a high multiplier for a base metal like copper. Alloys just seemed like a less efficient and tedious strategy to build.
For these reasons, alloys have been reworked to have their value based on the value of their ingredients. More formally, the value of an alloy is the sum of its ingredients with an additional ten coins. If a Copper Bar is worth 20 coins and a Gold Bar is worth 30 coins, then a Rose Gold Bar would be worth 60 coins. The Ultimate Alloy was also considered, and its value, when formed in the Alloy Smelter, is based on the value of the alloys used to make it. Ultimate Alloy found in Pandora's Box will have a base value of 100 coins, while other alloys still have their values based on their ingredients. With this, alloys become a much more profitable line of income as they have the potential to increase their value through multiple cards instead of one.

Fabricator Adjustment
Previously, the Fabricator was capable of copying Crates, including the items it contained. Although this was originally intended, it completely eliminated the need to create an automated setup.
To avoid this, the Fabricator was adjusted to create a copy as if it had just been purchased from the Shop. It is still free of cost, but the copied block will not have any information from the target transferred to it.


Card Changes
New Cards
Extra Gunpowder
As mentioned above, this card is targeted towards the Cannon. It increases the cannon's projectile's speed at the cost of increasing the chance of a misfire. When a misfire occurs, the Cannon appears to fire, but the item stays in the barrel and the fuse timer resets. This encourages players to limit how many of these cards they take since the chance for misfire can eventually make the Cannon completely useless.

Overclocking
As mentioned above, this card is targeted towards the Teleporter. It increases the speed at which the Teleporter charges up at the cost of increasing how long it takes to cool down. When a teleporter is cooling down, it cannot accept Items from outside blocks, but it can still receive an Item from its pair. This encourages players to use teleporters as a two-way exchange, where items enter and exit from both of the paired teleporters.

Card Changes
Squeaky Clean -> Laser Cutting
The recently released card "Squeaky Clean" was a card targeted at the Polisher. It increased its working speed at the cost of doubling its price in the Shop. However, it can be agreed that just having the price of the block doubled is unintuitive and boring. As a result, instead of increasing the cost, the card now increases the chance of the Polisher destroying its gem after processing.

Endless Grind
The card "Endless Grind" is a card targeted at the Grindstone. It increased the number of hits per use of the sharpened tool at the cost of doubling its price and increasing the hits required to apply sharpness. However, the double debuff seemed unfair and only discouraged the use of the Grindstone. As a result, the card now only increases the number of hits required to apply sharpness.


Quality of Life Changes
Tutorial

Extra precautions now prevent players from purchasing blocks during the tutorial, which softlocks them.
Extra precautions now prevent players from rerolling more than once during the tutorial, which softlocks them.  


Miscellaneous

Added a Room Pop-up Tip in the Main Menu to help guide new players to each room.
Added a new Block Attribute: Custom Text for blocks that have a chance of something happening (Cannon, Polisher, etc.)
Added borders to walls when the Low-Quality setting is active to aid visibility.



Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug allowing players to build on the row of tiles adjacent to the shop.
Adjusted any Particle Systems on blocks to be more compatible with Dynamite.
Fixed a bug where the content of Crates wouldn't be saved.
Fixed a bug where copied blocks weren't saved until the next round.
Fixed a bug where saving and exiting after restarting a run would bring back certain parts of the previous run.



Thanks for reading the Patch 1.2.0 Notes! With new content comes new bugs, so please report them if you find them! 

Best of luck,
Blue Muffin

notes.title: Patch 1.1.0
notes.notes:
Balance Changes
New Polisher Card: Squeaky Clean
A new card targeted at the Polisher was added. The card doubles the Polisher's operation speed at the cost of doubling the Polisher's price.

Ghosts
To balance out the difficulty of each challenge in Pure Chaos, the ghosts spawned by the Ghosts challenge have been adjusted.

Ghost Movement Speed: 5 m/s > 10 m/s
Time Between Seek Calls: 3s > 1.5s
Time to Haunt Item: 2s > 1s
Default Time Between Spawns: 15s > 7.5s
Decreased Time Between Spawns per Challenge: 5s > 2.5s

In short, Ghosts will now spawn more frequently, move faster, and steal items faster. The time between each ghost spawn is reduced, but the effect of each additional ghost challenge is reduced. These changes were made in hopes of increasing the threat of ghosts in the early game, since they are almost no threat in the late game.

Falling Rocks
To balance out the difficulty of each challenge in Pure Chaos, the Fallings Rocks challenge has been adjusted.

Rocks now spawn directly over a random player
Default Time Between Spawns: 15s > 7.5s
Decreased Time Between Spawns per Challenge: 5s > 2.5s

In short, Falling Rocks will spawn more frequently, but the effect of each additional falling rocks challenge is reduced. Falling rocks will spawn directly above a random player, forcing players to stay alert and move when necessary.

Stone Variants
The Stone Variants (Calcite, Granite, Limestone, Marble, and Stone) proved to be too weak compared to other sources of profit. As a result, the value of each Stone Variant item was increased slightly.

Stone Variant Chunks Value: 2c > 3c
Stone Variant Bricks Value: 6c > 8c

In short, Stone Variant items had their values increased in hopes of increasing their usefulness in runs.

Use Speed
Prior to this patch, the players' mining speed felt sluggish, which made it difficult to execute specific strategies. Also, the regular mining speed was incomparable to the speed of the "animation canceling" method that was discovered during Beta Testing.

Attempting "animation canceling" now results in a cooldown equal to the duration of the amount of time "canceled"
Time Between Uses: 1s > 0.83s

This creates a middle ground between those who use regular mining and those who use "animation canceling". This change was made in hopes of increasing the number of the players' potential strategies.

Rerolling
Prior to this patch, the rerolling system proved to be too expensive, even with easier difficulties. The price increased by 5 coins for each reroll, and the price only decreased after a round where players didn't use a reroll.

The price increment amount now varies by difficulty. (Easy: 2c, Medium: 3c, Hard: 4c, Impossible: 5c)
The price decreases after a round where players reroll less than 3 times
When the price decreases, it decreases more when fewer rerolls are used 
 
These changes were made to promote the rerolling system and make the difficulty level of each run more accurate to its set difficulty. Although rerolling is now cheaper, the price reduction system encourages players to limit how many rerolls they use each round.


Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where the character's rotation would freeze
Improved Conveyor behavior with specific and odd timings
Fixed a bug where a player could get stuck outside of the room on round start
Fixed a bug where players could place objects in the shop
Fixed a bug where a player could delete another player in Creative
Fixed odd camera sliding in Local Multiplayer Creative
Fixed Pop-Up Tip Down Version's screen position
Added extra measures to ensure the character's scale is appropriate
Added extra measures to prevent Compact Credits from being reduced caused by irregular coin values
Adjusted the automatic control scheme switcher to avoid switching when Keyboard (Right) is selected
Fixed a bug where rebinds for Keyboard (Right) movement inputs wouldn't save properly


Save System Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where stock in the Shop wasn't purchasable after returning from a save
Fixed object duplication
Fixed a bug where the center block in the room was a "ghost" block after returning from a save
Fixed the current reroll count resetting in each save
Added extra measures to prevent players from picking up a different block when loading their saved inventory
Fixed a bug where the walls would be missing after returning from a save before the first round



Quality of Life Changes

The Unlock Room pop-up tip's text now has a bold and italic portion to highlight the importance
The Unlock Room pop-up tip now appears again if the player attempts to unlock an object of a locked rarity
The animation speed of the Corner Conveyor and 3-1 Conveyor were increased to better match their transfer speeds
